outcome: ranitidine umbilical cord (arterial and venous) concentrations
umbilical cord arterial to venous ranitidine concentration ratios
cohort: Forty-one pregnant women scheduled for elective cesarean section, divided into healthy control (n=15), hypertension (n=16), and gestational diabetes (n=10) groups.
finding: Ranitidine maternal and umbilical cord concentrations, feto:maternal ratios, and maternal pharmacokinetic parameters (volume of distribution, clearance, half-life) were similar across all groups, indicating that hypertension and diabetes did not significantly affect ranitidine placental permeation or fetal handling.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken after ranitidine application, at delivery during elective cesarean section, and after delivery.
